title: Reported contract savings can shift spending rather than remove the underlying need
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office GAO-26-109096 review of Department of Homeland Security contract terminations and reported potential cost avoidance
geography: United States; Department of Homeland Security contracts, with a large reported share tied to information-technology indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contracts

denominator.unit: DHS contracts completely or partially terminated for convenience

reported_potential_avoidance.unit: DHS public estimate of current and future contract costs potentially avoided

observations.method: GAO analysis of federal procurement data, DHS documents, executive orders, agency guidance, and interviews with DHS procurement and financial officials.
observations.uncertainty: The reported potential avoidance is a maximum contract-value projection, not a forecast of what would otherwise have been obligated or a measure of realized savings.
observations.subgroup: DHS contracts terminated during the reviewed period; the reported estimate is concentrated in information-technology IDIQ contracts.
observations.counterinterpretation: Some terminations may still reduce future obligations, remove unnecessary work, or improve purchasing even when similar requirements are later bought through another contract.

denominator.unit: terminated IDIQ contracts accounting for 95% of DHS's reported potential cost avoidance

substituted_obligations.unit: fiscal-year 2025 obligations through existing government-wide contracts for the same requirements

realization_boundary.value: most of the reported $10.5 billion potential avoidance was unlikely to materialize

observations.method: GAO compared terminated DHS IDIQ contracts with subsequent obligations through existing government-wide contracts and reviewed the remaining contract period through fiscal year 2034.
observations.uncertainty: The comparison shows replacement spending and weakens the savings claim; it does not estimate the full counterfactual cost of continuing each terminated contract or the quality of the replacement service.
observations.subgroup: DHS information-technology requirements represented by the 30 IDIQ contracts.
observations.counterinterpretation: A replacement contract could produce better terms, service, or competition; replacement spending alone does not prove that termination was harmful.

denominator.unit: DHS contract decisions and replacement procurements; no linked service-user or worker denominator

visible_action.value: contract termination and deobligation were easier to report than whether the underlying mission need disappeared

unmeasured_outcomes.value: service continuity, contractor or worker effects, mission performance, and public experience were not measured in this review

observations.method: Interpretation bounded to GAO's procurement and obligation analysis; no inference is made about individual contracts beyond the reported subset and no same-service-user outcome is constructed.
observations.uncertainty: The record cannot show whether any particular termination improved efficiency, disrupted service, changed employment, or altered public trust.
observations.subgroup: Federal procurement and agency-capacity decisions rather than households or individual workers.
observations.counterinterpretation: Public reporting of a termination may be politically meaningful even when the fiscal effect is uncertain; symbolic reduction and operational savings are separate outcomes.

related_sources.claim: Official GAO accessible report supplies the contract counts, deobligations, projected avoidance, and replacement-obligation comparison.

boundary: This record shows a gap between announced or reported fiscal savings and realized reduction in underlying public obligations: a terminated contract can be replaced by another route. It does not establish whether any individual service, worker, vendor, mission, household, or community was better or worse off.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official GAO product page used for the extracted findings; the accessible PDF is linked as a related source.
